availableCommands.name: context-gatherer
availableCommands.description: Investigates the codebase to answer a specific question about it. Deeply analyzes existing code by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture and abstraction layers, understanding patterns, and documenting dependencies, returning a thorough, direct written analysis that explains how the relevant code works and points to the specific files and lines involved. Use it to understand code before you change it: before designing or implementing a change to code you don't already fully understand, start with context-gatherer so your edits are grounded in how the code actually works. When a task requires understanding code you don't already know, dispatch context-gatherer to do that exploration before running your own searches or reads. Rules: 1. Provide a clear, specific prompt that includes your intent: a detailed task description of the context you need and what you're trying to accomplish. 2. The subagent explores the codebase and returns an analysis of your query 3. Trust the returned results. You may still inspect additional code yourself when you need context beyond what was returned. 4. Reuse existing context-gatherer output for related follow-up questions; do not re-invoke on the same question with different phrasing. 5. For multiple distinct questions, dispatch several context-gatherers in parallel, each targeting a different aspect of the codebase.

# 02 · Standards and dashboard design for BusLink Studio

Written 2026-11-12. Two research agents read the sources listed at the end (transcript: `history://StandardsAndDashboardDesign`) but failed before writing. This brief condenses those sources and standard practice.
- Contrast ratios are **computed** with the WCAG 2.x relative-luminance formula.
- Figures from paywalled standards come from public previews or vendor/ISA summaries, and are marked as such.

---

## 1. High-performance HMI: ANSI/ISA-101.01-2015 and ASM Consortium

**What the standard and guidance say:**
- ISA-101 covers the HMI life cycle: philosophy, style guide, display hierarchy, and use of color. Its "high-performance" approach, popularised by the ASM Consortium and ISA's overview paper, has these traits:
  - **Grey, low-saturation background.** The screen is quiet when everything is normal.
  - **Color reserved for abnormal states.** Red and orange mean alarms; they are never decoration, and color is never the only cue.
  - **Analog indicators** show the value against its normal operating range and its alarm limits (a moving bar with shaded bands), instead of bare numbers.
  - **A display hierarchy:**
    - Level 1: overview, KPIs and trends.
    - Level 2: unit control.
    - Level 3: detail / equipment.
    - Level 4: diagnostics.
  - **Trends embedded** where a decision is made. Operators judge direction and rate of change faster from a sparkline than from a number.
- Rockwell, Honeywell/ASM and Inductive Automation publish similar rules ("Design like a pro"). [INFERENCE] There is no conflict between those sources.

**Palette.** The ratios below are computed (WCAG 2.2: text needs 4.5:1, non-text and large text need 3:1).

| Use | Foreground on background | Ratio | OK for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Base text (light) | `#1F1F1F` on `#D9D9D9` | 11.68:1 | all text |
| Secondary text (light) | `#4D4D4D` on `#D9D9D9` | 5.99:1 | all text |
| Panel text (light) | `#1F1F1F` on `#ECECEC` | 13.95:1 | all text |
| Normal trend line | `#6B6B6B` on `#D9D9D9` | 3.78:1 | non-text (lines) |
| **P1 alarm** fill, white text | `#FFFFFF` on `#CC3311` | 5.19:1 | text in badge |
| P1 alarm border/icon on base | `#CC3311` on `#D9D9D9` | 3.67:1 | non-text only |
| **P2 alarm** fill, black text | `#000000` on `#EE7733` | 7.32:1 | text in badge |
| **P3 alarm** fill, black text | `#000000` on `#F0E442` | 15.88:1 | text in badge |
| Selected / info fill, white text | `#FFFFFF` on `#0077BB` | 4.82:1 | text in badge |
| Info icon on base | `#0077BB` on `#D9D9D9` | 3.42:1 | non-text only |
| **Bad quality** fill, white text | `#FFFFFF` on `#AA3377` | 6.09:1 | text in badge |
| Bad quality icon on base | `#AA3377` on `#D9D9D9` | 4.31:1 | non-text / large text |
| Base text (dark) | `#E6E6E6` on `#2B2B2B` | 11.34:1 | all text |
| Secondary (dark) | `#B3B3B3` on `#2B2B2B` | 6.75:1 | all text |
| P1 alarm text (dark) | `#EE6677` on `#2B2B2B` | 4.59:1 | text |
| P3 alarm text (dark) | `#CCBB44` on `#2B2B2B` | 7.25:1 | text |
| Info text (dark) | `#66CCEE` on `#2B2B2B` | 7.71:1 | text |
| Bad quality text (dark) | `#CC79A7` on `#2B2B2B` | 4.63:1 | text |

The hues come from Paul Tol's colour-blind-safe schemes (`#CC3311`, `#EE7733`, `#0077BB`, `#EE3377`/`#AA3377`) and Okabe–Ito (`#F0E442`, `#CC79A7`).

**BusLink rules**
- Default theme is light ISA grey `#D9D9D9`, with text `#1F1F1F`. Dark mode is optional (`#2B2B2B`).
- Normal values render in neutral greys. Only abnormal states (alarm, bad quality, stale) get hue.
- Every live tile has: tag name, value, unit, a quality text label, data age, and a horizontal analog bar with a shaded normal band and alarm limit ticks. A sparkline of the last 5 minutes is optional.
- Alarm priority is shown by **shape + number + color**: P1 red triangle "1", P2 orange diamond "2", P3 yellow square "3". The shape and number carry the meaning; color is redundant.
- **Navigation follows the four display levels:**
  - L1: Overview (all devices, KPIs, active alarms).
  - L2: Device.
  - L3: Tag detail and trend.
  - L4: Register inspector and link diagnostics.
- No 3D gauges, no animated decoration, no gradients on data elements.

---

## 2. Alarm management: ANSI/ISA-18.2-2016 / IEC 62682:2022 / EEMUA 191 (4th ed.)

**Alarm states.** The ISA-18.2 state model, as summarised by ICONICS and the IEC 62682 preview:
- Normal
- **Unacknowledged** (active, not acked)
- **Acknowledged** (active, acked)
- **Return-to-normal unacknowledged** (cleared but not acked)
- **Shelved** (manually suppressed by the operator, with an expiry)
- **Suppressed by design** (by logic or state)
- **Out of service** (maintenance)

Latching alarms stay active until acknowledged.

**Performance targets.** Figures are from ISA and EEMUA summaries (ISA ie KPI paper, ProcessVue, Siemens white paper):
- Average alarm rate per operator: about 1 per 10 minutes is "very likely acceptable"; about 2 per 10 minutes is "maximum manageable".
- **Flood:** more than 10 alarms per 10 minutes.
- Priority distribution: about **80 % low / 15 % medium / 5 % high**.
- Standing alarms: under 5. Chattering alarms (≥ 3 in 1 minute) are a defect to fix.

**Deadband and delay starting points** (ISA-18.2 practice tables, cited in vendor guides):

| Process variable | Deadband | On/off delay |
|---|---|---|
| Flow, level | 5 % of range | 15 s |
| Pressure | 2 % | 15 s |
| Temperature | 1 % | 60 s |

**BusLink rules**
- **Alarm definition:** tag, type (HI/HIHI/LO/LOLO/ROC/quality), limit, deadband, on-delay, off-delay, priority (1–3), message, latch flag.
- **Engine:** implements the seven states above, including shelve-with-expiry and out-of-service. Alarms stay active while acknowledged.
- **Communication alarms** (timeout, CRC, disconnected) are a separate class from **process alarms**, so a dead link does not raise a flood of process alarms.
- **Alarm banner:**
  - Shows the count per priority and the oldest unacknowledged alarm.
  - The alarm list is sortable and filterable.
  - Acknowledge and shelve are logged events.
- A **flood indicator** appears when more than 10 alarms occur in 10 minutes. A chattering detector flags any alarm that fires 3 or more times in 1 minute.
- Default deadbands follow the table above, by unit type in the profile.

---

## 3. Data quality, timestamps and historians

- **OPC UA StatusCode** (Part 4 §7.38): the top two bits give the severity, Good `00`, Uncertain `01`, Bad `10`. Sub-codes include `Uncertain_LastUsableValue`, `Bad_NoCommunication`, `Bad_CommunicationError`, `Bad_Timeout`, `Bad_DecodingError` and `Bad_OutOfService`. The full list is in OPCFoundation `StatusCode.csv`.
- **Timestamps:** a DataValue carries a **SourceTimestamp** (when the value was measured or sampled at the source) and a **ServerTimestamp** (when the server received it). For Modbus, the source timestamp is when the response arrived, because devices carry no time.
- **Ignition** shows quality overlays on bad or stale tags (`Bad_Stale`, `Uncertain_LastKnownValue`, `Bad_NotConnected`).
- **PI** stores data with exception filtering plus swinging-door compression, and records digital states such as "I/O Timeout" or "Comm Fail" so trends show gaps.
- **Grafana and InfluxDB** render nulls as **gaps** unless "connect null values" is enabled. `aggregateWindow(createEmpty: true)` keeps empty windows as nulls.

**Quality mapping:**

| BusLink quality | OPC UA equivalent | UI treatment | Trend |
|---|---|---|---|
| GOOD | Good | neutral; age shown in grey | line |
| STALE (last good older than 3× the poll interval) | Uncertain_LastUsableValue | value greyed + "STALE · 12 s" + hatched tile edge | gap after the last good point |
| TIMEOUT | Bad_Timeout | magenta "TIMEOUT" badge; keep the last value struck through | gap |
| CRC_ERROR | Bad_CommunicationError | magenta "CRC" badge | gap |
| EXCEPTION(n) | Bad_DeviceFailure / Bad_NotSupported (by code) | magenta "EXC 02 Illegal address" | gap |
| DECODE_ERROR | Bad_DecodingError | magenta "DECODE" | gap |
| DISCONNECTED | Bad_NoCommunication | whole device card greyed + "DISCONNECTED" | gap |

**BusLink rules**
- Every sample stores both timestamps (`ts_src` = response time, `ts_rx` = time stored) plus quality and `age_ms`.
- Trends **never interpolate across non-GOOD samples**: draw `null` and show the gap. The tooltip on a gap states the reason.
- Exports include `quality`, `quality_opcua` (numeric code) and `age_ms` columns.
- Logging can apply a configurable deadband per tag (a value is recorded when |Δ| > deadband or the heartbeat interval passes). Raw polling still feeds the live view.

---

## 4. MQTT 5 and Sparkplug B 3.0 (ISO/IEC 20237:2023)

- **MQTT 5** (OASIS) adds message expiry, session expiry, will delay, topic aliases and reason codes. These help for intermittent links such as phones.
- **Sparkplug B 3.0:**
  - **Namespace:** `spBv1.0/{group_id}/{NBIRTH|NDEATH|NDATA|NCMD|DBIRTH|DDEATH|DDATA|DCMD}/{edge_node_id}[/{device_id}]`, plus `spBv1.0/STATE/{host_id}`.
  - **Payload:** protobuf metrics with aliases.
  - **Sequencing:** `seq` cycles 0–255 per edge node, and `bdSeq` ties BIRTH to DEATH.
  - **Store-and-forward:** uses a "historical" flag.
  - Published as ISO/IEC 20237:2023.
- **Fit for a phone or laptop gateway.** Sparkplug gives state awareness: the broker's will message publishes DEATH when the gateway drops. The costs are protobuf, a BIRTH/rebirth flow, and alias management. For a hackathon MVP with ad-hoc brokers, plain JSON topics are easier to test with any MQTT client. [INFERENCE]

**BusLink rules**
- **MVP** publishes MQTT 5 plain JSON on `buslink/{site}/{gateway}/{device}/{tag}`, with payload `{ts, seq, value, unit, quality, profile_version}`. The gateway has a retained `buslink/{site}/{gateway}/status` = `online|offline`, and the will message sets `offline`.
- Messages with expiry use QoS 1. The offline outbox is bounded and replayed with the original `ts` and `seq`; consumers deduplicate on `(gateway, seq)`.
- **No commands over MQTT** in the competition build (telemetry only).
- **Sparkplug B is post-MVP:** generate NBIRTH/DBIRTH from the profile and send DDATA by alias.

---

## 5. Security: IEC 62443 and Modbus/TCP Security

- **IEC 62443 security levels:**
  - SL1: casual or coincidental violation.
  - SL2: intentional, simple means.
  - SL3: sophisticated means.
  - SL4: extended resources.
- **Foundational requirements:**
  - FR1: identification and authentication.
  - FR2: use control.
  - FR3: system integrity.
  - FR4: data confidentiality.
  - FR5: restricted data flow.
  - FR6: timely response to events.
  - FR7: resource availability.
- **Relevant 62443-4-2 component requirements:**
  - CR 1.1: human user identification and authentication.
  - CR 2.1: authorization=<redacted>  - CR 2.8: auditable events.
  - CR 3.1: communication integrity.
  - CR 4.1: information confidentiality.
- **Zones and conduits:** the tool sits on the engineering side, and the RS485 bus is its own zone.
- **Modbus/TCP Security** (Modbus.org): TLS 1.2+ on **port 802**, mutual X.509 authentication, and an X.509 v3 **role extension** carrying a role used for authorization. Legacy Modbus TCP (port 502) has no authentication.

**BusLink rules**
- **Read-only by default (FR2).** Writes need explicit arming per device, with a session timeout, and go through the command service only.
- An audit record for every arm, write, read-back, acknowledge and shelve (CR 2.8). Each record carries the user/session, device, profile version, and request/response hex.
- **LAN dashboard (FR4/FR5):**
  - Off by default; binds to one chosen interface.
  - Uses TLS (self-signed per session) plus a random token.
  - Read-only routes, no write endpoints; rate-limited.
- **Secrets** (MQTT passwords) go in the OS keychain or Android Keystore. They never appear in profiles, projects, exports or logs.
- **Profiles are data only.** They are validated against a JSON Schema, and expressions are limited to scale/offset; no scripts.
- Modbus/TCP Security (port 802) is a later transport option and is out of scope for the MVP. The docs must say so clearly.

---

## 6. Modbus protocol and serial line facts

**Application Protocol V1.1b3 limits:**
- FC01/02: 1–2000 bits.
- FC03/04: 1–125 registers.
- FC05: single coil, FF00/0000.
- FC06: single register.
- FC15: 1–1968 bits.
- FC16: 1–123 registers.
- FC23: read 125 / write 121.
- The PDU is at most 253 bytes; the RTU ADU at most 256 bytes.

**Exception codes:**

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 01 | Illegal function |
| 02 | Illegal data address |
| 03 | Illegal data value |
| 04 | Server device failure |
| 05 | Acknowledge |
| 06 | Server busy |
| 08 | Memory parity error |
| 0A | Gateway path unavailable |
| 0B | Gateway target failed to respond |

**Serial Line Guide V1.02:**
- RTU frames are separated by ≥ 3.5 character times, and a gap > 1.5 character times inside a frame is an error. Above 19200 baud, fixed values are recommended: **t1.5 = 750 µs, t3.5 = 1.75 ms**.
- Default 8E1 (19200 even parity is the spec default); 8N2 when there is no parity. 8N1 is common in practice but non-standard.
- Unit addresses 1–247; 0 is broadcast (writes only, no reply).
- **RS-485 physical layer** (Serial Line Guide + TI SLLA272):
  - 120 Ω termination at **both ends** of the trunk only.
  - Fail-safe biasing at one point.
  - Up to 32 unit loads per segment.
  - About 1200 m at low baud rates.
  - Daisy chain with short stubs.
  - Common/ground reference conductor.

**Word order** (Modbus Poll naming): `ABCD` (big-endian), `CDAB` (word-swapped), `BADC` (byte-swapped), `DCBA` (little-endian).

**BusLink rules**
- **Scheduler:** splits reads at the FC limits above.
- **RTU parser:** uses the expected length (from the function code and byte count), with inter-frame silence as a secondary check. It applies t3.5 = max(3.5 chars, 1.75 ms).
- **Unit ID 0:** writes to it are rejected in the UI and by the guard hook.
- **Exceptions:** shown as code + name + a likely-cause hint.
- **Inspector:** shows all four word orders side by side; the user chooses one, and it is saved in the profile.
- **Wiring help page:** termination at both ends, biasing, A/B naming differences between vendors, the separate sensor power supply, and the fact that the Waveshare (B) board is non-isolated.

---

## 7. Time-series charting library

Bundle sizes are minified + gzip from the bundlephobia API, read by the earlier agent. Treat them as approximate.

| Library | Size | Many points / streaming | Gaps | Decimation | Multi-axis | License |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **uPlot** | ~20 KB | Very fast canvas; 100k+ points; `setData` append | `null` → gap (spanGaps off) | none built in (do min-max yourself) | yes | MIT |
| Apache ECharts 5/6 | ~330 KB+ (tree-shaken less) | Good; `large`, `progressive`, `appendData` | `connectNulls:false` | `sampling: 'lttb' \| 'minmax' \| 'average'` | yes | Apache-2.0 |
| Chart.js 4 | ~70 KB | Fair; slower at 100k | `spanGaps` | decimation plugin (LTTB, min-max) | yes | MIT |
| Plotly.js | ~1 MB+ | Heavy; WebGL traces help | `connectgaps` | none | yes | MIT |
| lightweight-charts | ~45 KB | Fast | whitespace data | none | limited price scales | Apache-2.0 + attribution |

**Notes on the options:**
- lightweight-charts spaces bars evenly by index, not proportionally to time (issues #1342, #847). That breaks irregular polling intervals.
- **Min-max/M4 decimation** (Jugel et al., VLDB 2014) keeps extreme values pixel-accurate. LTTB (Steinarsson 2013) looks smooth but can drop spikes. Spikes matter for alarms.

**BusLink rules**
- Use **uPlot** for trends. It is small for the Android WebView, fast, handles `null` gaps natively, and works with real timestamps.
- Decimate with **min-max per pixel column** on the Rust side for long ranges; it works with the historian's minute rollups. Never use LTTB for alarm-relevant data.
- **Gaps:** non-GOOD samples become `null`, and a shaded band marks the gap with its reason.
- **Overlays:** alarm limits are horizontal bands; acknowledge and write events are vertical markers.
- **Axes:** one y-axis per unit, at most 2 per chart; tags with other units go in additional charts.
- UI refresh is throttled to ≤ 4 Hz, independent of the polling rate.

---

## 8. Accessibility and colour vision

- **WCAG 2.2 AA requirements:**
  - **1.4.3** text contrast 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text, ≥ 18.66 px bold or ≥ 24 px).
  - **1.4.11** non-text contrast 3:1 for UI components and graphics.
  - **1.4.1** colour is not the only means of conveying information.
  - **2.5.8** target size at least 24×24 CSS px (new in 2.2).
  - **4.1.3** status messages announced without moving focus.
  - **2.2.2** moving or updating content that starts automatically and lasts more than 5 s needs pause/stop/hide unless it is essential.
  - **1.3.4** no orientation lock.
- **Colour vision deficiency:** about **8 % of men** and 0.5 % of women of Northern European ancestry have red–green deficiency (MedlinePlus/NEI). That is why red-versus-green status alone fails.

**BusLink rules**
- Use the palette in §1. Every status has a **text label** ("TIMEOUT", "P1") and a **shape**.
- **Live regions:** alarms and connection changes go to an `aria-live="polite"` region; P1 alarms use `assertive`.
- **Pause:** a "Pause live updates" control freezes the dashboard values for reading or screenshots (2.2.2).
- **Touch targets:** ≥ 24 px everywhere and 44 px for primary mobile actions (connect, arm, stop).
- **Keyboard:** all controls are reachable. Focus rings are visible (`#0077BB`, 3:1 against the base).
- **Motion and orientation:** respect `prefers-reduced-motion` (no pulsing alarms; use a static border instead). Portrait and landscape both work.

---

## Sources

1. ISA, *The High Performance HMI* overview v2.01: https://www.isa.org/getmedia/06130a38-f7af-4b35-8c9c-2c34f25c1977/The-High-Performance-HMI-Overview-v2-01.pdf
2. ANSI/ISA-101.01-2015 preview: https://webstore.ansi.org/preview-pages/ISA/preview_ANSI+ISA+101.01-2015.pdf; ISA-101 standards page: https://www.isa.org/standards-and-publications/isa-standards/isa-101-standards
3. Inductive Automation, *Design like a pro*: https://inductiveautomation.com/resources/article/design-like-a-pro-optimizing-your-hmi
4. Control Global, high-performance HMI rules: https://img.controlglobal.com/files/base/ebm/controlglobal/document/2022/08/1661879878912-cg1709highperformancehmirules…
5. IEC 62682:2022 preview: https://assets.vde-verlag.de/iec-normen/preview-pdf/info_iec62682%7Bed2.0.CMV%7Den.pdf
6. ICONICS alarm state transition diagram: https://documentation.iconics.com/v10.98/Content/Alarming/Alarm%20Server/Alarm%20References/alarm-state-transition-diag…
7. Alarm System Performance Metrics (ISA Ireland): https://isa.ie/wp-content/uploads/2016/06/Alarm_System_Performance_Metrics_Kim_Van_camp.pdf

# 02 · Standards and dashboard design for BusLink Studio

Written 2026-11-12. Two research agents read the sources listed at the end (transcript: `history://StandardsAndDashboardDesign`) but failed before writing. This brief condenses those sources and standard practice.
- Contrast ratios are **computed** with the WCAG 2.x relative-luminance formula.
- Figures from paywalled standards come from public previews or vendor/ISA summaries, and are marked as such.

---

## 1. High-performance HMI: ANSI/ISA-101.01-2015 and ASM Consortium

**What the standard and guidance say:**
- ISA-101 covers the HMI life cycle: philosophy, style guide, display hierarchy, and use of color. Its "high-performance" approach, popularised by the ASM Consortium and ISA's overview paper, has these traits:
  - **Grey, low-saturation background.** The screen is quiet when everything is normal.
  - **Color reserved for abnormal states.** Red and orange mean alarms; they are never decoration, and color is never the only cue.
  - **Analog indicators** show the value against its normal operating range and its alarm limits (a moving bar with shaded bands), instead of bare numbers.
  - **A display hierarchy:**
    - Level 1: overview, KPIs and trends.
    - Level 2: unit control.
    - Level 3: detail / equipment.
    - Level 4: diagnostics.
  - **Trends embedded** where a decision is made. Operators judge direction and rate of change faster from a sparkline than from a number.
- Rockwell, Honeywell/ASM and Inductive Automation publish similar rules ("Design like a pro"). [INFERENCE] There is no conflict between those sources.

**Palette.** The ratios below are computed (WCAG 2.2: text needs 4.5:1, non-text and large text need 3:1).

| Use | Foreground on background | Ratio | OK for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Base text (light) | `#1F1F1F` on `#D9D9D9` | 11.68:1 | all text |
| Secondary text (light) | `#4D4D4D` on `#D9D9D9` | 5.99:1 | all text |
| Panel text (light) | `#1F1F1F` on `#ECECEC` | 13.95:1 | all text |
| Normal trend line | `#6B6B6B` on `#D9D9D9` | 3.78:1 | non-text (lines) |
| **P1 alarm** fill, white text | `#FFFFFF` on `#CC3311` | 5.19:1 | text in badge |
| P1 alarm border/icon on base | `#CC3311` on `#D9D9D9` | 3.67:1 | non-text only |
| **P2 alarm** fill, black text | `#000000` on `#EE7733` | 7.32:1 | text in badge |
| **P3 alarm** fill, black text | `#000000` on `#F0E442` | 15.88:1 | text in badge |
| Selected / info fill, white text | `#FFFFFF` on `#0077BB` | 4.82:1 | text in badge |
| Info icon on base | `#0077BB` on `#D9D9D9` | 3.42:1 | non-text only |
| **Bad quality** fill, white text | `#FFFFFF` on `#AA3377` | 6.09:1 | text in badge |
| Bad quality icon on base | `#AA3377` on `#D9D9D9` | 4.31:1 | non-text / large text |
| Base text (dark) | `#E6E6E6` on `#2B2B2B` | 11.34:1 | all text |
| Secondary (dark) | `#B3B3B3` on `#2B2B2B` | 6.75:1 | all text |
| P1 alarm text (dark) | `#EE6677` on `#2B2B2B` | 4.59:1 | text |
| P3 alarm text (dark) | `#CCBB44` on `#2B2B2B` | 7.25:1 | text |
| Info text (dark) | `#66CCEE` on `#2B2B2B` | 7.71:1 | text |
| Bad quality text (dark) | `#CC79A7` on `#2B2B2B` | 4.63:1 | text |

The hues come from Paul Tol's colour-blind-safe schemes (`#CC3311`, `#EE7733`, `#0077BB`, `#EE3377`/`#AA3377`) and Okabe–Ito (`#F0E442`, `#CC79A7`).

**BusLink rules**
- Default theme is light ISA grey `#D9D9D9`, with text `#1F1F1F`. Dark mode is optional (`#2B2B2B`).
- Normal values render in neutral greys. Only abnormal states (alarm, bad quality, stale) get hue.
- Every live tile has: tag name, value, unit, a quality text label, data age, and a horizontal analog bar with a shaded normal band and alarm limit ticks. A sparkline of the last 5 minutes is optional.
- Alarm priority is shown by **shape + number + color**: P1 red triangle "1", P2 orange diamond "2", P3 yellow square "3". The shape and number carry the meaning; color is redundant.
- **Navigation follows the four display levels:**
  - L1: Overview (all devices, KPIs, active alarms).
  - L2: Device.
  - L3: Tag detail and trend.
  - L4: Register inspector and link diagnostics.
- No 3D gauges, no animated decoration, no gradients on data elements.

---

## 2. Alarm management: ANSI/ISA-18.2-2016 / IEC 62682:2022 / EEMUA 191 (4th ed.)

**Alarm states.** The ISA-18.2 state model, as summarised by ICONICS and the IEC 62682 preview:
- Normal
- **Unacknowledged** (active, not acked)
- **Acknowledged** (active, acked)
- **Return-to-normal unacknowledged** (cleared but not acked)
- **Shelved** (manually suppressed by the operator, with an expiry)
- **Suppressed by design** (by logic or state)
- **Out of service** (maintenance)

Latching alarms stay active until acknowledged.

**Performance targets.** Figures are from ISA and EEMUA summaries (ISA ie KPI paper, ProcessVue, Siemens white paper):
- Average alarm rate per operator: about 1 per 10 minutes is "very likely acceptable"; about 2 per 10 minutes is "maximum manageable".
- **Flood:** more than 10 alarms per 10 minutes.
- Priority distribution: about **80 % low / 15 % medium / 5 % high**.
- Standing alarms: under 5. Chattering alarms (≥ 3 in 1 minute) are a defect to fix.

**Deadband and delay starting points** (ISA-18.2 practice tables, cited in vendor guides):

| Process variable | Deadband | On/off delay |
|---|---|---|
| Flow, level | 5 % of range | 15 s |
| Pressure | 2 % | 15 s |
| Temperature | 1 % | 60 s |

**BusLink rules**
- **Alarm definition:** tag, type (HI/HIHI/LO/LOLO/ROC/quality), limit, deadband, on-delay, off-delay, priority (1–3), message, latch flag.
- **Engine:** implements the seven states above, including shelve-with-expiry and out-of-service. Alarms stay active while acknowledged.
- **Communication alarms** (timeout, CRC, disconnected) are a separate class from **process alarms**, so a dead link does not raise a flood of process alarms.
- **Alarm banner:**
  - Shows the count per priority and the oldest unacknowledged alarm.
  - The alarm list is sortable and filterable.
  - Acknowledge and shelve are logged events.
- A **flood indicator** appears when more than 10 alarms occur in 10 minutes. A chattering detector flags any alarm that fires 3 or more times in 1 minute.
- Default deadbands follow the table above, by unit type in the profile.

---

## 3. Data quality, timestamps and historians

- **OPC UA StatusCode** (Part 4 §7.38): the top two bits give the severity, Good `00`, Uncertain `01`, Bad `10`. Sub-codes include `Uncertain_LastUsableValue`, `Bad_NoCommunication`, `Bad_CommunicationError`, `Bad_Timeout`, `Bad_DecodingError` and `Bad_OutOfService`. The full list is in OPCFoundation `StatusCode.csv`.
- **Timestamps:** a DataValue carries a **SourceTimestamp** (when the value was measured or sampled at the source) and a **ServerTimestamp** (when the server received it). For Modbus, the source timestamp is when the response arrived, because devices carry no time.
- **Ignition** shows quality overlays on bad or stale tags (`Bad_Stale`, `Uncertain_LastKnownValue`, `Bad_NotConnected`).
- **PI** stores data with exception filtering plus swinging-door compression, and records digital states such as "I/O Timeout" or "Comm Fail" so trends show gaps.
- **Grafana and InfluxDB** render nulls as **gaps** unless "connect null values" is enabled. `aggregateWindow(createEmpty: true)` keeps empty windows as nulls.

**Quality mapping:**

| BusLink quality | OPC UA equivalent | UI treatment | Trend |
|---|---|---|---|
| GOOD | Good | neutral; age shown in grey | line |
| STALE (last good older than 3× the poll interval) | Uncertain_LastUsableValue | value greyed + "STALE · 12 s" + hatched tile edge | gap after the last good point |
| TIMEOUT | Bad_Timeout | magenta "TIMEOUT" badge; keep the last value struck through | gap |
| CRC_ERROR | Bad_CommunicationError | magenta "CRC" badge | gap |
| EXCEPTION(n) | Bad_DeviceFailure / Bad_NotSupported (by code) | magenta "EXC 02 Illegal address" | gap |
| DECODE_ERROR | Bad_DecodingError | magenta "DECODE" | gap |
| DISCONNECTED | Bad_NoCommunication | whole device card greyed + "DISCONNECTED" | gap |

**BusLink rules**
- Every sample stores both timestamps (`ts_src` = response time, `ts_rx` = time stored) plus quality and `age_ms`.
- Trends **never interpolate across non-GOOD samples**: draw `null` and show the gap. The tooltip on a gap states the reason.
- Exports include `quality`, `quality_opcua` (numeric code) and `age_ms` columns.
- Logging can apply a configurable deadband per tag (a value is recorded when |Δ| > deadband or the heartbeat interval passes). Raw polling still feeds the live view.

---

## 4. MQTT 5 and Sparkplug B 3.0 (ISO/IEC 20237:2023)

- **MQTT 5** (OASIS) adds message expiry, session expiry, will delay, topic aliases and reason codes. These help for intermittent links such as phones.
- **Sparkplug B 3.0:**
  - **Namespace:** `spBv1.0/{group_id}/{NBIRTH|NDEATH|NDATA|NCMD|DBIRTH|DDEATH|DDATA|DCMD}/{edge_node_id}[/{device_id}]`, plus `spBv1.0/STATE/{host_id}`.
  - **Payload:** protobuf metrics with aliases.
  - **Sequencing:** `seq` cycles 0–255 per edge node, and `bdSeq` ties BIRTH to DEATH.
  - **Store-and-forward:** uses a "historical" flag.
  - Published as ISO/IEC 20237:2023.
- **Fit for a phone or laptop gateway.** Sparkplug gives state awareness: the broker's will message publishes DEATH when the gateway drops. The costs are protobuf, a BIRTH/rebirth flow, and alias management. For a hackathon MVP with ad-hoc brokers, plain JSON topics are easier to test with any MQTT client. [INFERENCE]

**BusLink rules**
- **MVP** publishes MQTT 5 plain JSON on `buslink/{site}/{gateway}/{device}/{tag}`, with payload `{ts, seq, value, unit, quality, profile_version}`. The gateway has a retained `buslink/{site}/{gateway}/status` = `online|offline`, and the will message sets `offline`.
- Messages with expiry use QoS 1. The offline outbox is bounded and replayed with the original `ts` and `seq`; consumers deduplicate on `(gateway, seq)`.
- **No commands over MQTT** in the competition build (telemetry only).
- **Sparkplug B is post-MVP:** generate NBIRTH/DBIRTH from the profile and send DDATA by alias.

---

## 5. Security: IEC 62443 and Modbus/TCP Security

- **IEC 62443 security levels:**
  - SL1: casual or coincidental violation.
  - SL2: intentional, simple means.
  - SL3: sophisticated means.
  - SL4: extended resources.
- **Foundational requirements:**
  - FR1: identification and authentication.
  - FR2: use control.
  - FR3: system integrity.
  - FR4: data confidentiality.
  - FR5: restricted data flow.
  - FR6: timely response to events.
  - FR7: resource availability.
- **Relevant 62443-4-2 component requirements:**
  - CR 1.1: human user identification and authentication.
  - CR 2.1: authorization=<redacted>  - CR 2.8: auditable events.
  - CR 3.1: communication integrity.
  - CR 4.1: information confidentiality.
- **Zones and conduits:** the tool sits on the engineering side, and the RS485 bus is its own zone.
- **Modbus/TCP Security** (Modbus.org): TLS 1.2+ on **port 802**, mutual X.509 authentication, and an X.509 v3 **role extension** carrying a role used for authorization. Legacy Modbus TCP (port 502) has no authentication.

**BusLink rules**
- **Read-only by default (FR2).** Writes need explicit arming per device, with a session timeout, and go through the command service only.
- An audit record for every arm, write, read-back, acknowledge and shelve (CR 2.8). Each record carries the user/session, device, profile version, and request/response hex.
- **LAN dashboard (FR4/FR5):**
  - Off by default; binds to one chosen interface.
  - Uses TLS (self-signed per session) plus a random token.
  - Read-only routes, no write endpoints; rate-limited.
- **Secrets** (MQTT passwords) go in the OS keychain or Android Keystore. They never appear in profiles, projects, exports or logs.
- **Profiles are data only.** They are validated against a JSON Schema, and expressions are limited to scale/offset; no scripts.
- Modbus/TCP Security (port 802) is a later transport option and is out of scope for the MVP. The docs must say so clearly.

---

## 6. Modbus protocol and serial line facts

**Application Protocol V1.1b3 limits:**
- FC01/02: 1–2000 bits.
- FC03/04: 1–125 registers.
- FC05: single coil, FF00/0000.
- FC06: single register.
- FC15: 1–1968 bits.
- FC16: 1–123 registers.
- FC23: read 125 / write 121.
- The PDU is at most 253 bytes; the RTU ADU at most 256 bytes.

**Exception codes:**

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 01 | Illegal function |
| 02 | Illegal data address |
| 03 | Illegal data value |
| 04 | Server device failure |
| 05 | Acknowledge |
| 06 | Server busy |
| 08 | Memory parity error |
| 0A | Gateway path unavailable |
| 0B | Gateway target failed to respond |

**Serial Line Guide V1.02:**
- RTU frames are separated by ≥ 3.5 character times, and a gap > 1.5 character times inside a frame is an error. Above 19200 baud, fixed values are recommended: **t1.5 = 750 µs, t3.5 = 1.75 ms**.
- Default 8E1 (19200 even parity is the spec default); 8N2 when there is no parity. 8N1 is common in practice but non-standard.
- Unit addresses 1–247; 0 is broadcast (writes only, no reply).
- **RS-485 physical layer** (Serial Line Guide + TI SLLA272):
  - 120 Ω termination at **both ends** of the trunk only.
  - Fail-safe biasing at one point.
  - Up to 32 unit loads per segment.
  - About 1200 m at low baud rates.
  - Daisy chain with short stubs.
  - Common/ground reference conductor.

**Word order** (Modbus Poll naming): `ABCD` (big-endian), `CDAB` (word-swapped), `BADC` (byte-swapped), `DCBA` (little-endian).

**BusLink rules**
- **Scheduler:** splits reads at the FC limits above.
- **RTU parser:** uses the expected length (from the function code and byte count), with inter-frame silence as a secondary check. It applies t3.5 = max(3.5 chars, 1.75 ms).
- **Unit ID 0:** writes to it are rejected in the UI and by the guard hook.
- **Exceptions:** shown as code + name + a likely-cause hint.
- **Inspector:** shows all four word orders side by side; the user chooses one, and it is saved in the profile.
- **Wiring help page:** termination at both ends, biasing, A/B naming differences between vendors, the separate sensor power supply, and the fact that the Waveshare (B) board is non-isolated.

---

## 7. Time-series charting library

Bundle sizes are minified + gzip from the bundlephobia API, read by the earlier agent. Treat them as approximate.

| Library | Size | Many points / streaming | Gaps | Decimation | Multi-axis | License |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **uPlot** | ~20 KB | Very fast canvas; 100k+ points; `setData` append | `null` → gap (spanGaps off) | none built in (do min-max yourself) | yes | MIT |
| Apache ECharts 5/6 | ~330 KB+ (tree-shaken less) | Good; `large`, `progressive`, `appendData` | `connectNulls:false` | `sampling: 'lttb' \| 'minmax' \| 'average'` | yes | Apache-2.0 |
| Chart.js 4 | ~70 KB | Fair; slower at 100k | `spanGaps` | decimation plugin (LTTB, min-max) | yes | MIT |
| Plotly.js | ~1 MB+ | Heavy; WebGL traces help | `connectgaps` | none | yes | MIT |
| lightweight-charts | ~45 KB | Fast | whitespace data | none | limited price scales | Apache-2.0 + attribution |

**Notes on the options:**
- lightweight-charts spaces bars evenly by index, not proportionally to time (issues #1342, #847). That breaks irregular polling intervals.
- **Min-max/M4 decimation** (Jugel et al., VLDB 2014) keeps extreme values pixel-accurate. LTTB (Steinarsson 2013) looks smooth but can drop spikes. Spikes matter for alarms.

**BusLink rules**
- Use **uPlot** for trends. It is small for the Android WebView, fast, handles `null` gaps natively, and works with real timestamps.
- Decimate with **min-max per pixel column** on the Rust side for long ranges; it works with the historian's minute rollups. Never use LTTB for alarm-relevant data.
- **Gaps:** non-GOOD samples become `null`, and a shaded band marks the gap with its reason.
- **Overlays:** alarm limits are horizontal bands; acknowledge and write events are vertical markers.
- **Axes:** one y-axis per unit, at most 2 per chart; tags with other units go in additional charts.
- UI refresh is throttled to ≤ 4 Hz, independent of the polling rate.

---

## 8. Accessibility and colour vision

- **WCAG 2.2 AA requirements:**
  - **1.4.3** text contrast 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text, ≥ 18.66 px bold or ≥ 24 px).
  - **1.4.11** non-text contrast 3:1 for UI components and graphics.
  - **1.4.1** colour is not the only means of conveying information.
  - **2.5.8** target size at least 24×24 CSS px (new in 2.2).
  - **4.1.3** status messages announced without moving focus.
  - **2.2.2** moving or updating content that starts automatically and lasts more than 5 s needs pause/stop/hide unless it is essential.
  - **1.3.4** no orientation lock.
- **Colour vision deficiency:** about **8 % of men** and 0.5 % of women of Northern European ancestry have red–green deficiency (MedlinePlus/NEI). That is why red-versus-green status alone fails.

**BusLink rules**
- Use the palette in §1. Every status has a **text label** ("TIMEOUT", "P1") and a **shape**.
- **Live regions:** alarms and connection changes go to an `aria-live="polite"` region; P1 alarms use `assertive`.
- **Pause:** a "Pause live updates" control freezes the dashboard values for reading or screenshots (2.2.2).
- **Touch targets:** ≥ 24 px everywhere and 44 px for primary mobile actions (connect, arm, stop).
- **Keyboard:** all controls are reachable. Focus rings are visible (`#0077BB`, 3:1 against the base).
- **Motion and orientation:** respect `prefers-reduced-motion` (no pulsing alarms; use a static border instead). Portrait and landscape both work.

# UI rules (webview + LAN dashboard)

TODO: `research/02-standards-and-dashboard-design.md` was not available when this file was written (2026-11-11). These rules come from ISA-101 / WCAG 2.2 basics and the owner's brief. Revise this file when that research lands.

## ISA-101 high-performance style

- **Gray, calm normal state.** Neutral light-gray background, dark-gray text and outlines, no saturated color when everything is normal. No 3D, gradients, photos or decorative animation.
- **Color means abnormal.** Saturated colors are reserved for alarms and abnormal quality, and every colored state also has a text label and a shape or icon. Never use green for "running" or "OK"; normal needs no color.
- Values show number + unit + quality. Use analog indicators (bar with normal range band, setpoint marker) where position matters more than digits.
- Hierarchy: overview (all devices, worst state first) → device page (tags) → detail (trend, register inspector).
- Project color tokens (ISA-101 does not mandate exact RGB values; check every pair with a contrast checker):

| Token | Use | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `--bg` | page background | light neutral gray |
| `--surface` | tiles, tables | slightly lighter/darker gray than `--bg` |
| `--text`, `--text-muted` | values, labels | ≥ 4.5:1 on `--surface`; muted only for secondary text, still ≥ 4.5:1 |
| `--alarm-1` (critical) | red | badge with white or dark text ≥ 4.5:1 |
| `--alarm-2` (high) | orange/amber | dark text on fill |
| `--alarm-3` (low/advisory) | yellow | dark text on fill; never yellow text on gray |
| `--quality-bad` | comm/quality problems | distinct from process alarm colors (e.g. magenta or cyan outline + hatch) |
| `--focus` | focus ring | ≥ 3:1 against adjacent colors |

- Process alarms (value out of limits) and communication problems (quality) look different and are listed separately.

## Quality display

- Every value shows its quality. GOOD shows the value plainly. Any other quality shows a text badge (`TIMEOUT`, `CRC`, `EXC 02`, `STALE`, `DECODE`) and the age ("12 s ago"), plus a non-color cue (hatched background or outlined value).
- STALE / failed values show the **last good value dimmed with its age**, never as a current reading, never as 0 and never blank without explanation.
- Tiles show data age and the poll interval actually achieved. A device header shows link state separately from value quality.
- The register inspector shows, per row: table, doc address (manual label), PDU offset, FC, raw hex, decoded value in the profile's word order, all four word orders on demand, quality and exception text.

## Trends

- **Gaps are gaps.** Any sample that is not GOOD breaks the line (pass `null`); never interpolate, draw connecting lines or carry the last value forward across lost communication. Shade comm-loss intervals with a hatched band and label it ("No data: TIMEOUT").
- Keep raw samples separate from display resampling. When downsampling, draw min/max bands, not just averages, and say which one is shown.
- Show alarm limits as bands, setpoint as a line, time axis in local time with UTC in tooltips/exports.
- Throttle rendering (UI refresh independent of poll rate, ≤ 4 fps for trends on Android) to save battery.

## Control panel (simulated devices only)

- Banner "Simulated device" on every control view. Armed state is obvious (border + text "Armed: control enabled for 52 s").
- Buttons name the action and value: "Apply setpoint 40 °C". The confirm dialog shows device, unit ID, register (doc address + offset), old → new, raw value and encoded frame.
- Separate fields for command sent, acknowledged, and measured feedback; show pending/unknown honestly.
- Every stop control carries the label "Software stop. Not an emergency stop." / "Stop perangkat lunak. Bukan tombol darurat."
- The LAN dashboard build renders no control panel, no write UI and no arming controls at all.

## Accessibility (WCAG 2.2 AA)

- Contrast: text ≥ 4.5:1 (large text ≥ 3:1); UI components, chart lines and focus indicators ≥ 3:1 (1.4.3, 1.4.11).
- Never color alone (1.4.1): text label + shape/pattern for every state; trends distinguish series by dash pattern or markers too.
- Fully keyboard operable, visible focus that is not hidden by sticky headers (2.1.1, 2.4.7, 2.4.11). Logical heading and tab order.
- Pointer targets ≥ 24×24 CSS px (2.5.8). **Android: ≥ 48×48 dp** with ≥ 8 dp spacing; destructive or control actions never sit next to each other.
- Live value updates must not flood screen readers: use `aria-live="polite"` only for alarms and connection changes, not for every sample.
- `prefers-reduced-motion`: no blinking or animated transitions; alarm flashing becomes a static marker. Nothing flashes more than 3 times per second (2.3.1).
- Reflow at 320 CSS px wide and 200% zoom without losing content (1.4.10, 1.4.4). Support system dark mode only if both themes pass contrast.
- Form errors are announced in text next to the field (3.3.1); confirmation dialogs trap and restore focus.

## i18n (id / en)

- All strings in `src/i18n/en.json` and `src/i18n/id.json` with the same keys; a missing key is a test failure. Default language follows the system, switchable at runtime, persisted.
- Units and technical symbols are identical in both languages (°C, %RH, µS/cm, FC03, CRC). Terms like "register", "holding register", "unit ID" may stay English in Indonesian text when that is what technicians use.
- Display numbers in the active locale (id uses decimal comma), but exports always use `.` decimals and ISO-8601 UTC.
- Set `lang` on `<html>`; text may grow ~30% in Indonesian, so no fixed-width labels.

## Security in the UI

- Render profile, device and user strings with `textContent` or escaped templates; never `innerHTML` with data.
- Never show secrets (MQTT password, LAN token) after entry except an explicit "show" toggle; QR/URL for LAN sharing is shown only on the host device.

</content>
</file>

# BusLink Studio: epics and sprint plan (BMAD phase 3–4)

Each epic becomes one Kiro feature spec in `.kiro/specs/<epic>/` and is executed by the `buslink-builder` agent. `ics-security-reviewer` reviews every epic commit, and the builder fixes its findings.

| # | Epic (Kiro spec) | PRD | Done when | Target (WIB) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| E1 | `core-protocol`: RTU/TCP framing, CRC, codec, profile schema, quality model, scheduler, fake transport, property tests | R4–R9, R7 | `cargo test` green; PBT for CRC/framing/codec/order; dead-device fairness test | Nov 13 |
| E2 | `simulator`: in-process soil/VFD/temp/energy devices, fault injection, loopback RTU + TCP server | R10, R24 | Sim drives all E1 tests; VFD/temp state machines respond to writes | Nov 14 |
| E3 | `app-shell-desktop`: Tauri 2 app, Windows serial transport (VID:PID detect), sample bus, historian, CSV/XLSX/JSON export | R1, R3, R12, R20, R21 | Windows exe reads the simulator + the real BGT-SMPS on the CH343G; export opens in Excel | Nov 17 |
| E4 | `dashboard-ui`: connection center, ISA-101 live tiles, uPlot gap-aware trends, register inspector, alarms, i18n id/en, training mode | R12–R16, R24, N3, N4 | Headless Chrome journey 1 passes; WCAG checks; 360 px layout | Nov 21 |
| E5 | `commissioning-control`: command service state machine, ID/baud wizard, simulated VFD/temperature control panel, audit, reports | R17–R19, N1 | Journey 4 passes; the guard hook blocks writes outside `command/` | Nov 24 |
| E6 | `android-otg`: Kotlin USB plugin (usb-serial-for-android), permission, FGS, SAF export, APK | R2 | APK reads the real sensor on the A35 via OTG (journey 2) | Nov 26 |
| E7 | `lan-mqtt`: axum read-only LAN dashboard (token + TLS), MQTT 5 telemetry with outbox | R22, R23 | Journeys 3 and 5 pass | Nov 28 |
| E8 | `release`: NSIS + portable exe, APK, README/judge guide, evidence matrix, Remotion video, SolidCraft 3D, submission kit | N5, N6 | Release published; video < 3 min; Devpost submitted | Dec 2 |

**Readiness gate:** PASS.
- PRD, architecture and research are complete, and the hardware is available.
- **Risk to watch:** E6 (Android USB) is the largest unknown. Its spike task runs early, right after E1/E3, so it is never left to the last week.

</content>
</file>

<content>
# BusLink Studio: PRD (BMAD phase 2)

Inputs: `product-brief.md`, `research/00-owner-research-brief.pdf`, `research/01-competitors-and-features.md`, `research/02-standards-and-dashboard-design.md`, `research/03-platform-tauri-android-usb.md`.
Status: approved scope "plus-control" (owner, 2026-11-11). Each requirement has an ID that the Kiro spec cites.

## 1. Goals and non-goals
**Goals:** one Modbus workbench on Windows, Android (USB OTG) and a LAN browser view, sharing one profile format. Data quality and data age are always visible. Writes are safe. Judges can try everything with a simulator.

**Non-goals (competition):**
- Cloud accounts, payments, Play Store publishing.
- Driving a real VFD or heater (simulator profiles only).
- Writes from the LAN browser.
- Linux/macOS builds. Tauri supports them, but they are untested here.

## 2. Users and top jobs
| User | Job | Pain it removes (research/01) |
|---|---|---|
| Commissioning technician | Connect a new device, find the right registers, check the values, hand over a report | #1 addressing, #2 word order, #3 unknown serial settings, #4 wiring vs software |
| Maintenance in the field | Check a device on the plant floor with only a phone | #10 fragile Android apps; no shared profile between PC and phone |
| Supervisor / trainer | Watch live values on any screen; run a lab without hardware | #9 stale values look healthy; labs need a simulator |
| Integrator | Change unit ID/baud or a setpoint safely, with a record | #7 unsafe writes |

## 3. Functional requirements
### Connectivity
- **R1 RTU desktop:** Windows COM ports. Detect WCH adapters by VID:PID (CH343 1A86:55D3 as inbox CDC-ACM, CH340 1A86:7523, CH9102 1A86:55D4), not by friendly name. Baud 300–3 000 000, data 7/8, parity N/E/O, stop 1/2.
- **R2 RTU Android:** USB OTG with a permission flow. Rotation keeps the session (state lives in the Rust core). A `connectedDevice` foreground service keeps polling with the screen off. Detach → DISCONNECTED, and nothing auto-resumes writes. Target API 36.
- **R3 Modbus TCP:** MBAP with transaction IDs, reconnect with backoff, unit ID. RTU-over-TCP is a separate transport type.
- **R4 One master per bus:** one scheduler queue per link. One failing device never blocks the others (backoff on it).

### Protocol and data
- **R5 Function codes:** FC01/02/03/04 read; FC05/06/15/16 write. Spec limits: 125 registers (FC03/04), 2000 coils, 123 registers (FC16). Merge contiguous reads into blocks.
- **R6 Codec:** U16/I16/U32/I32/U64/I64/F32/F64, bit fields, string. Word/byte order ABCD/CDAB/BADC/DCBA, stored explicitly in the profile. Scale, offset, unit, decimals, valid range, sentinel values.
- **R7 Quality:** every sample carries GOOD / TIMEOUT / CRC_ERROR / EXCEPTION(code) / STALE / DECODE_ERROR / DISCONNECTED, plus `age_ms`, source timestamp and receive timestamp. Last-good values are shown as stale, never as fresh. (OPC UA Good/Uncertain/Bad mapping per research/02.)
- **R8 Addressing:** always show the manual/documentation address *and* the PDU offset. Never send 40001-style numbers raw.

### Profiles
- **R9 Device profile:** JSON, versioned, schema-validated. Holds identity, serial defaults, register blocks, tags (address, FC, type, order, scale, unit, range, writable, min/max write), commands, and a support level: `generic | documented | simulated | hardware_verified` with source (manual and page). Profiles and device instances are separate.
- **R10 Bundled profiles:**
  - BGT-SMPS 8-in-1 soil sensor (`documented`, upgraded to `hardware_verified` after the real test).
  - Simulated VFD (`simulated`).
  - Simulated temperature controller (`simulated`).
  - Simulated energy meter (`simulated`).
  - A generic holding-register template.
- **R11 Import:** CSV/XLSX register map with preview and address-base detection. `.mbmap` read-only import (P2).

### UI
- **R12 Connection center:** ports/adapters, USB permission state, serial settings, TCP host, link statistics (TX/RX, CRC, timeouts, cycle time).
- **R13 Live dashboard:** ISA-101 high-performance style (grey base, color only for abnormal states, analog bar with normal range). Tiles show value, unit, quality text and age. Density toggle; Indonesian and English.
- **R14 Trends:** multiple tags with unit axes, cursor, zoom. **Gaps for lost communication, never interpolated.** Raw samples separate from display decimation (min-max). Alarm bands.
- **R15 Register inspector:** doc address, PDU offset, raw hex, decoded value in all four orders side by side, and the last request/response frame.
- **R16 Alarms (ISA-18.2):** threshold, hysteresis/deadband, on/off delay, priority, acknowledge, shelve with expiry. Communication alarms kept separate from process alarms. Alarm log.
- **R17 Commissioning wizard:** change unit ID or baud on one device, with journal → write → reconnect at the new settings → read-back → pass/fail. A recovery hint shows the old settings.
- **R18 Control panel (simulated VFD + temperature controller):**
  - The command service requires the device to be armed (session timeout), checks bounds, and asks for confirmation with an explicit label ("Apply setpoint 40.0 °C").
  - It encodes a frame preview, writes once (no automatic retry), reads back, and records the audit entry.
  - A software stop is always reachable and labeled "not an E-stop".
- **R19 Reports:** session summary (devices, profile versions, quality statistics, alarms, commands) exported as PDF/HTML.

### Data
- **R20 Historian:** SQLite WAL with tables sessions, devices, tags, samples, events, commands, outbox. Logging interval separate from polling interval. Retention setting.
- **R21 Export:** CSV (UTF-8, ISO-8601 UTC, quality and age columns, formula-injection guard), XLSX (Measurements, Devices, Configuration, Events, Commands sheets, numbers kept as numbers), JSON. Android saves through SAF.

### Sharing
- **R22 LAN dashboard:** opt-in. The app serves the same frontend (read-only routes + WebSocket stream) on a user-chosen interface/port, with a per-session token, TLS (self-signed per session; the URL/QR carries the token), and no write endpoints. Works from Windows and Android.
- **R23 MQTT telemetry:** opt-in. MQTT 5 over TLS, topic `buslink/{site}/{gateway}/{device}/{tag}` or a Sparkplug-B-compatible namespace (decision in architecture), payload with ts/seq/value/unit/quality/profile_version, a bounded offline outbox, deduplication by sequence. Credentials go in the OS secret store and never into project files.

### Training
- **R24 Simulator:** built-in multi-device RTU-over-loopback and TCP simulator with the bundled simulated profiles. Fault injection: timeout, CRC error, exception, stale, wrong word order. A **training mode** with guided exercises in Indonesian and English.

## 4. Non-functional requirements
- **N1 Safety:** read-only by default. Writes only through the command service. No broadcast writes. Audit trail for every command.
- **N2 Security:** IEC 62443-minded. LAN and MQTT off by default. Tokens + TLS. Profiles are data only (no scripts). No secrets in exports or logs. CSV formula guard.
- **N3 Performance (targets, to be measured):** UI keeps 60 fps with 50 tags at 1 Hz. Trend of 100k points renders in under 1 s on desktop. Android stays responsive at 10 tags/s.
- **N4 Accessibility:** WCAG 2.2 AA. Status shown as text plus color. Keyboard operation on desktop. Touch targets ≥ 24 CSS px (AA), with 44 px on primary mobile actions. Reduced motion.
- **N5 Packaging:** Windows NSIS installer (WebView2 bootstrapper) + portable exe. Android APK (arm64). SHA-256 sums.
- **N6 Evidence:** a separate pass/fail matrix for simulator and for hardware. A profile becomes `hardware_verified` only with recorded evidence.

## 5. Acceptance (demo)
1. Fresh Windows install → Training mode → read 3 simulated devices → trend shows a gap when a fault is injected → export XLSX with quality columns.
2. Real BGT-SMPS sensor through the CH343G adapter on Windows, then the same profile on the Samsung A35 via OTG. Values match within one poll.
3. Browser on the LAN shows the phone's live dashboard, read-only.
4. Simulated VFD: arm → set frequency 30.0 Hz → read-back OK → stop → audit log entry.
5. MQTT: messages arrive at a local broker with sequence numbers; disconnect → outbox → replay without duplicates.

</content>
</file>

- **R1 RTU desktop:** Windows COM ports. Detect WCH adapters by VID:PID (CH343 1A86:55D3 as inbox CDC-ACM, CH340 1A86:7523, CH9102 1A86:55D4), not by friendly name. Baud 300–3 000 000, data 7/8, parity N/E/O, stop 1/2.
- **R2 RTU Android:** USB OTG with a permission flow. Rotation keeps the session (state lives in the Rust core). A `connectedDevice` foreground service keeps polling with the screen off. Detach → DISCONNECTED, and nothing auto-resumes writes. Target API 36.
- **R3 Modbus TCP:** MBAP with transaction IDs, reconnect with backoff, unit ID. RTU-over-TCP is a separate transport type.
- **R4 One master per bus:** one scheduler queue per link. One failing device never blocks the others (backoff on it).

### Protocol and data
- **R5 Function codes:** FC01/02/03/04 read; FC05/06/15/16 write. Spec limits: 125 registers (FC03/04), 2000 coils, 123 registers (FC16). Merge contiguous reads into blocks.
- **R6 Codec:** U16/I16/U32/I32/U64/I64/F32/F64, bit fields, string. Word/byte order ABCD/CDAB/BADC/DCBA, stored explicitly in the profile. Scale, offset, unit, decimals, valid range, sentinel values.
- **R7 Quality:** every sample carries GOOD / TIMEOUT / CRC_ERROR / EXCEPTION(code) / STALE / DECODE_ERROR / DISCONNECTED, plus `age_ms`, source timestamp and receive timestamp. Last-good values are shown as stale, never as fresh. (OPC UA Good/Uncertain/Bad mapping per research/02.)
- **R8 Addressing:** always show the manual/documentation address *and* the PDU offset. Never send 40001-style numbers raw.

### Profiles
- **R9 Device profile:** JSON, versioned, schema-validated. Holds identity, serial defaults, register blocks, tags (address, FC, type, order, scale, unit, range, writable, min/max write), commands, and a support level: `generic | documented | simulated | hardware_verified` with source (manual and page). Profiles and device instances are separate.
- **R10 Bundled profiles:**
  - BGT-SMPS 8-in-1 soil sensor (`documented`, upgraded to `hardware_verified` after the real test).
  - Simulated VFD (`simulated`).
  - Simulated temperature controller (`simulated`).
  - Simulated energy meter (`simulated`).
  - A generic holding-register template.
- **R11 Import:** CSV/XLSX register map with preview and address-base detection. `.mbmap` read-only import (P2).

### UI
- **R12 Connection center:** ports/adapters, USB permission state, serial settings, TCP host, link statistics (TX/RX, CRC, timeouts, cycle time).
- **R13 Live dashboard:** ISA-101 high-performance style (grey base, color only for abnormal states, analog bar with normal range). Tiles show value, unit, quality text and age. Density toggle; Indonesian and English.
- **R14 Trends:** multiple tags with unit axes, cursor, zoom. **Gaps for lost communication, never interpolated.** Raw samples separate from display decimation (min-max). Alarm bands.
- **R15 Register inspector:** doc address, PDU offset, raw hex, decoded value in all four orders side by side, and the last request/response frame.
- **R16 Alarms (ISA-18.2):** threshold, hysteresis/deadband, on/off delay, priority, acknowledge, shelve with expiry. Communication alarms kept separate from process alarms. Alarm log.
- **R17 Commissioning wizard:** change unit ID or baud on one device, with journal → write → reconnect at the new settings → read-back → pass/fail. A recovery hint shows the old settings.
- **R18 Control panel (simulated VFD + temperature controller):**
  - The command service requires the device to be armed (session timeout), checks bounds, and asks for confirmation with an explicit label ("Apply setpoint 40.0 °C").
  - It encodes a frame preview, writes once (no automatic retry), reads back, and records the audit entry.
  - A software stop is always reachable and labeled "not an E-stop".
- **R19 Reports:** session summary (devices, profile versions, quality statistics, alarms, commands) exported as PDF/HTML.

### Data
- **R20 Historian:** SQLite WAL with tables sessions, devices, tags, samples, events, commands, outbox. Logging interval separate from polling interval. Retention setting.
- **R21 Export:** CSV (UTF-8, ISO-8601 UTC, quality and age columns, formula-injection guard), XLSX (Measurements, Devices, Configuration, Events, Commands sheets, numbers kept as numbers), JSON. Android saves through SAF.

### Sharing
- **R22 LAN dashboard:** opt-in. The app serves the same frontend (read-only routes + WebSocket stream) on a user-chosen interface/port, with a per-session token, TLS (self-signed per session; the URL/QR carries the token), and no write endpoints. Works from Windows and Android.
- **R23 MQTT telemetry:** opt-in. MQTT 5 over TLS, topic `buslink/{site}/{gateway}/{device}/{tag}` or a Sparkplug-B-compatible namespace (decision in architecture), payload with ts/seq/value/unit/quality/profile_version, a bounded offline outbox, deduplication by sequence. Credentials go in the OS secret store and never into project files.

### Training
- **R24 Simulator:** built-in multi-device RTU-over-loopback and TCP simulator with the bundled simulated profiles. Fault injection: timeout, CRC error, exception, stale, wrong word order. A **training mode** with guided exercises in Indonesian and English.

## 4. Non-functional requirements
- **N1 Safety:** read-only by default. Writes only through the command service. No broadcast writes. Audit trail for every command.
- **N2 Security:** IEC 62443-minded. LAN and MQTT off by default. Tokens + TLS. Profiles are data only (no scripts). No secrets in exports or logs. CSV formula guard.
- **N3 Performance (targets, to be measured):** UI keeps 60 fps with 50 tags at 1 Hz. Trend of 100k points renders in under 1 s on desktop. Android stays responsive at 10 tags/s.
- **N4 Accessibility:** WCAG 2.2 AA. Status shown as text plus color. Keyboard operation on desktop. Touch targets ≥ 24 CSS px (AA), with 44 px on primary mobile actions. Reduced motion.
- **N5 Packaging:** Windows NSIS installer (WebView2 bootstrapper) + portable exe. Android APK (arm64). SHA-256 sums.
- **N6 Evidence:** a separate pass/fail matrix for simulator and for hardware. A profile becomes `hardware_verified` only with recorded evidence.

## 5. Acceptance (demo)
1. Fresh Windows install → Training mode → read 3 simulated devices → trend shows a gap when a fault is injected → export XLSX with quality columns.
2. Real BGT-SMPS sensor through the CH343G adapter on Windows, then the same profile on the Samsung A35 via OTG. Values match within one poll.
3. Browser on the LAN shows the phone's live dashboard, read-only.
4. Simulated VFD: arm → set frequency 30.0 Hz → read-back OK → stop → audit log entry.
5. MQTT: messages arrive at a local broker with sequence numbers; disconnect → outbox → replay without duplicates.

# BusLink Studio: architecture (BMAD phase 3) Covers the PRD requirement IDs (R1–R24, N1–N6). Technical facts are from `research/03-platform-tauri-android-usb.md`. ## Context ```mermaid flowchart LR subgraph Device["Windows PC / Android phone (one Tauri 2 app)"] UI[Web UI
TypeScript + uPlot] -- Tauri IPC --> Svc[App services] Svc --> Core[buslink-core
codec · scheduler · profiles · quality · command service] Core --> Tr{Transport trait} Tr --> SerW[Serial: Windows COM] Tr --> SerA[Serial: Android USB OTG] Tr --> TCP[Modbus TCP] Tr --> Sim[buslink-sim
in-process simulator] Core --> Hist[(SQLite historian)] Core --> Bus[Sample bus
broadcast channel] Bus --> UI Bus --> LAN[axum LAN server
read-only + WS] Bus --> MQ[MQTT publisher
outbox] end SerW & SerA --> RS485[USB-RS485 CH343G → RS485 bus → devices] TCP --> PLC[Modbus TCP devices] LAN --> Browser[LAN browser] MQ --> Broker[MQTT broker] ``` ## Repository layout ``` crates/buslink-core/ # protocol (RTU/TCP framing, CRC), codec, profile schema + validation, # scheduler (one queue per link), quality, alarms, command service, historian, export crates/buslink-sim/ # deterministic simulator: soil sensor, VFD, temperature controller, energy meter; fault injection src-tauri/ # Tauri shell: IPC commands, transports (Windows serial, Android USB), LAN server, MQTT src-tauri/gen/android/ # generated Android project + Kotlin USB permission / FGS src/ # web UI (TypeScript, Vite), shared by the desktop window, Android WebView and LAN browsers profiles/ # bundled device profiles (JSON) + schema video/ # Remotion demo video project docs/ # BMAD, design, verification, Kiro evidence ``` ## Key decisions | # | Decision | Alternatives | Why | |---|---|---|---| | D1 | **Own RTU/TCP framing in `buslink-core`**, reusing `rmodbus`-style pure codec ideas; no async transport crate in core | tokio-modbus | Core stays sync and testable with a fake transport (property tests on CRC/framing). Length-based RTU parsing (from FC and byte count) is robust against USB fragmentation on Android (research/03 risk table). | | D2 | **Transport trait** `open/configure/read(timeout)/write/flush/close` + detach event; implementations for Windows serial (`serialport`), Android USB (Kotlin usb-serial-for-android 3.12 via a Tauri mobile plugin, bytes bridged over JNI), TCP (std net), simulator (in-memory) | tauri-plugin-serialplugin 4.2 on both | The plugin is young (4 months). Our own Kotlin path is the proven pattern from the owner's earlier Android work. The trait lets us swap. | | D3 | **One worker thread per link** owns the transport; requests go through an mpsc queue with priorities (commands > alarms > polling); per-device backoff | async tasks | Matches "one master per bus" (R4). Blocking serial I/O stays off the tokio runtime. | | D4 | **Sample bus** = `tokio::sync::broadcast` of `Sample{device, tag, raw, value, unit, quality, age_ms, ts_source, ts_rx, seq, profile_version}` consumed by UI, historian, LAN, MQTT | each consumer polls | One source of truth; every consumer sees identical quality. | | D5 | **uPlot** for trends | ECharts, Chart.js | Small (~50 KB), fast for 100k+ points, supports null gaps natively. Final choice confirmed against research/02. | | D6 | **LAN server = axum** on the Tauri tokio runtime, bound to a chosen interface, self-signed cert per session (rcgen), token in URL/QR, only GET + WS routes | Tauri localhost plugin (no Android) | R22. There are no write routes at all, so nothing to misconfigure. | | D7 | **MQTT: plain JSON topics `buslink/{site}/{gw}/{device}/{tag}`** in the MVP; Sparkplug B later | Sparkplug B now | Sparkplug's protobuf/birth/death adds a lot for a phone gateway. Plain topics + seq + quality meet R23. Revisit after the MVP. | | D8 | **Command service** state machine: `Idle → Armed(timeout) → Previewed(frame) → Confirmed → Sent → ReadBack → Done/Failed`, single attempt, audit row per transition | direct writes | N1/R18. The only code path that may emit FC05/06/15/16 (enforced by a Kiro hook). | | D9 | **Historian**: SQLite WAL, batch inserts every 1 s, logging interval ≥ polling interval, min/max/avg rollups per minute for long trends | raw only | R20 and N3 (big ranges load quickly). | | D10 | **Android targetSdk 36**, minSdk 24, `connectedDevice` FGS started after USB permission | API 37 | Avoids the Android 17 local-network permission until it is handled (research/03). | | D11 | Windows packaging: NSIS with WebView2 bootstrapper + portable exe; Android arm64 APK (debug-signed for the hackathon) | MSI | NSIS works from our toolchain; MSI is not required. | ## Data model (historian) `sessions(id, started, app_version, platform)` · `devices(id, session, profile_id, profile_version, unit_id, link)` · `tags(id, device, key, unit)` · `samples(tag, ts_rx_ms, ts_src_ms, seq, raw BLOB, value REAL, quality INT, age_ms)` · `events(ts, kind, device, tag, severity, text)` · `commands(id, ts, device, fc, address, requested, encoded_hex, response_hex, readback, state, user_note)` · `outbox(seq, topic, payload, tries)` · rollups `samples_1m(tag, minute, n, min, max, sum)`. ## Security (N2) - **Threat surfaces:** the write path, LAN server, MQTT credentials, imported profiles/CSV, USB permission. - **Controls:** - A Kiro hook blocks write function codes outside `command/` and the simulator. - The LAN server has no write routes. - Profiles are data validated by JSON Schema (no expressions or scripts). - CSV export has a formula guard. - Secrets are kept in the OS keychain / Android Keystore. - **Default posture:** LAN and MQTT off until the user enables them. ## Test strategy - **Unit and property tests in `buslink-core`:** - CRC known vectors. - Encode→decode round trip for all FCs. - Decoder never panics on random bytes. - All word orders. - Quality transitions. - Command state machine. - Scheduler fairness with one dead device. - **Simulator integration tests:** multi-device poll, fault injection, gap rendering data. - **UI:** `tsc` + a headless Chrome check of the five acceptance journeys. - **Hardware:** an evidence matrix (Windows + CH343G + BGT-SMPS; Android A35 + OTG + BGT-SMPS).

Output:
# simulator: requirements

Epic E2 (`docs/bmad/epics-and-sprint.md`). Crate: `crates/buslink-sim`. Covers PRD R10 and R24, and supports N6 (simulator evidence is separate from hardware evidence).
Rules that always apply: `.kiro/steering/safety.md` (rule 12: simulator results never upgrade a profile), `.kiro/steering/modbus.md`.

## Requirement 1: in-process Modbus server (R24)

**User story:** As a judge or trainee without hardware, I want simulated devices that behave like Modbus slaves on a bus, so that every BusLink feature can be tried end to end.

1. THE simulator SHALL implement the server side of FC01, FC02, FC03, FC04, FC05, FC06, FC15 and FC16 for every simulated device.
2. WHEN a request addresses an unmapped register, THE simulator SHALL answer exception 02; WHEN a function is not supported by the device, exception 01; WHEN a quantity is outside the spec limits or a value is invalid for the device, exception 03.
3. WHEN a multi-register or multi-coil write touches any address that is not writable, THE simulator SHALL reject the whole request and change nothing.
4. WHEN an RTU request has a bad CRC or addresses a unit ID that no device has, THE simulator SHALL stay silent (as a real slave does).
5. WHEN a request uses unit ID 0 (broadcast), THE simulator SHALL apply writes to every device and SHALL NOT reply, matching the serial line spec. BusLink itself never sends it (safety rule 4).

## Requirement 2: transports (R24, R3)

1. THE simulator SHALL provide an in-memory transport implementing `buslink_core::transport::Transport` for RTU framing and for MBAP framing.
2. THE in-memory RTU transport SHALL be able to deliver responses in seeded random chunk sizes, so that USB-style fragmentation is exercised.
3. THE simulator SHALL provide a Modbus TCP server bound to a loopback address (default `127.0.0.1`, port chosen by the caller or the OS) that serves all simulated devices by unit ID, can be stopped, and never binds to `0.0.0.0` by default.
4. Response timing SHALL follow the shared clock, so tests with a manual clock never sleep.

## Requirement 3: BGT-SMPS soil sensor (R10)

1. THE simulator SHALL serve the BGT-SMPS 8-in-1 register map exactly as documented (holding registers 0–7: temperature i16 ÷ 10 °C, moisture u16 ÷ 10 %, EC u16 µS/cm, salinity u16, N/P/K u16 mg/kg, pH u16 ÷ 100), FC03 only, read-only.
2. Values SHALL drift realistically (bounded mean-reverting random walk) and deterministically for a given seed.
3. Registers outside 0–7 SHALL answer exception 02 (registers 8–9 are undocumented and not served).

## Requirement 4: simulated VFD (R10, R18)

1. THE VFD SHALL expose a control word (stop 0, run 1, reset fault 4), a frequency setpoint (0.00–50.00 Hz, ×100), output frequency, status word (running, at speed, fault bits), fault code, motor current and a ramp time.
2. WHEN running, the output frequency SHALL ramp toward the setpoint at the configured ramp rate; WHEN stopped, it SHALL ramp to zero.
3. WHEN a fault is active, run commands SHALL be acknowledged but the drive SHALL stay stopped until a reset while stopped clears the fault (acknowledged ≠ reached target).
4. Out-of-range setpoints and unknown control words SHALL answer exception 03.

## Requirement 5: simulated temperature controller (R10, R18)

1. THE controller SHALL expose PV, SP, output %, mode (auto/manual), manual output and heater enable.

`SimWorld::new(seed)` or `SimWorld::training(seed)` (soil 1, VFD 2, temperature 3, meter 4); `add_device(unit, model)`; each device gets its own `SplitMix64` seeded with `seed ^ (unit × golden ratio constant)`. `advance_to(now_ms)` runs `step(100 ms)` as many times as needed since the last step, so results do not depend on poll timing (Req 8.2). 1. Advance the world.

3. Evaluate the device's fault rules (first matching rule wins): timeout → no reply; exception → exception PDU; CRC → reply marked corrupt; late reply → `delay_ms`; stale and wrong order change how the image is produced.
4. Dispatch through `server.rs`.

| Model ID | Table | Registers (PDU offset) | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bgt_smps_8in1` | holding | 0 temp i16 ×0.1 °C, 1 moisture u16 ×0.1 %, 2 EC u16 µS/cm, 3 salinity u16, 4 N, 5 P, 6 K u16 mg/kg, 7 pH u16 ×0.01 | Ornstein–Uhlenbeck drift around plausible field values; FC03 only; read-only (writes → exception 01) |

THE simulator SHALL support per-device faults: timeout (no reply), CRC error (corrupted CRC; on MBAP a corrupted byte count), exception (given code), stale (values frozen while replies continue), wrong word order (multi-register values served word-swapped, 16-bit values byte-swapped), and late reply (reply after a delay).
2. Each fault SHALL have a trigger: always, a seeded probability, a time window, or a request-count window.
3. Faults SHALL be switchable at run time and SHALL never change the device's register map.

## Requirement 8: determinism (R24)

1. WHEN two simulator worlds are created with the same seed and receive the same requests at the same simulated times, THEY SHALL produce byte-identical responses.
2. Process models SHALL advance in fixed simulated time steps, independent of how often they are polled.

## Requirement 9: bundled profiles (R10, safety rule 12)

----
# simulator: design

Implements `requirements.md` in `crates/buslink-sim`, which depends on `buslink-core` (never the other way round).

## 1. Layout

```
crates/buslink-sim/src/
  lib.rs
  world.rs        SimWorld: devices by unit ID, faults, seed, fixed-step clock; handle_pdu / handle_rtu
  server.rs       request dispatch: read FCs via core ReadRequest, write FCs via core command::wire decoder
  image.rs        RegisterImage: sparse tables + writable sets; ImageBuilder with word-order fault
  fault.rs        FaultKind, Trigger, FaultRule, FaultTable
  transport.rs    SimTransport (in-memory, RTU or MBAP framing, seeded chunking)
  tcp.rs          SimTcpServer (std::net, loopback)
  devices/
    mod.rs        SimModel trait, model registry by simulator model ID
    soil.rs       BGT-SMPS 8-in-1
    vfd.rs        VFD
    temp.rs       temperature controller
    energy.rs     energy meter
crates/buslink-sim/tests/   integration tests that combine core + sim
```

## 2. Device model contract

```rust
trait SimModel: Send {
    fn model_id(&self) -> &'static str;
    fn step(&mut self, dt_ms: u64, rng: &mut SplitMix64);   // fixed step, 100 ms
    fn image(&self, wrong_order: bool) -> RegisterImage;    // registers as served now
    fn apply(&mut self, write: &WriteRequest) -> Result<(), ExceptionCode>;
}
```

`RegisterImage` holds four sparse tables and the set of writable addresses. The server answers reads from the image, so the register map is defined once per model. `ImageBuilder` encodes values with `buslink_core::codec`; with the wrong-order fault it serves 32/64-bit values word-swapped (`ABCD → CDAB`) and 16-bit values byte-swapped.

Writes: the server checks that every target address exists and is writable (exception 02 otherwise), then calls `apply` once with the whole request; models validate values (exception 03) before changing state, so a rejected request changes nothing.

## 3. World and time

`SimWorld::new(seed)` or `SimWorld::training(seed)` (soil 1, VFD 2, temperature 3, meter 4); `add_device(unit, model)`; each device gets its own `SplitMix64` seeded with `seed ^ (unit × golden ratio constant)`. `advance_to(now_ms)` runs `step(100 ms)` as many times as needed since the last step, so results do not depend on poll timing (Req 8.2). A device under the `stale` fault is not stepped (values frozen) but still answers.

`handle_pdu(unit, pdu, now_ms) -> Reply { pdu: Option<Vec<u8>>, delay_ms, corrupt: bool }`:
1. Advance the world.
2. Unit 0: apply writes to all devices, no reply. Unknown unit: no reply.
3. Evaluate the device's fault rules (first matching rule wins): timeout → no reply; exception → exception PDU; CRC → reply marked corrupt; late reply → `delay_ms`; stale and wrong order change how the image is produced.
4. Dispatch through `server.rs`.

## 4. Transports

`SimTransport::rtu(world, clock, chunking)` and `SimTransport::mbap(world, clock)` implement core `Transport`:
- `write_all` collects request bytes, frames RTU requests by function code (FC01–06: 8 bytes; FC15/16: `9 + byte count`; unknown FC: whole buffer), drops frames with bad CRC (silence), and queues the reply with `ready_at = now + turnaround + delay`. A corrupt reply flips CRC bits (RTU) or the byte count (MBAP).
- `read(buf, timeout)` returns queued bytes that are ready, waiting through `clock.sleep_ms` (a manual clock advances instantly); with nothing ready before the timeout it returns 0.
- Chunking: `Chunking::Whole` or `Chunking::Random { max, seed }` splits replies into 1..=max byte pieces.

`SimTcpServer::start(world, addr)` binds a `std::net::TcpListener` (loopback only unless the caller passes another address explicitly), accepts with a non-blocking poll loop, switches accepted sockets back to blocking (Windows inherits non-blocking mode from the listener), and serves one connection per thread with MBAP framing, a connection cap (8) and a 260-byte frame limit. `stop()` joins the threads.

## 5. Device models

| Model ID | Table | Registers (PDU offset) | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bgt_smps_8in1` | holding | 0 temp i16 ×0.1 °C, 1 moisture u16 ×0.1 %, 2 EC u16 µS/cm, 3 salinity u16, 4 N, 5 P, 6 K u16 mg/kg, 7 pH u16 ×0.01 | Ornstein–Uhlenbeck drift around plausible field values; FC03 only; read-only (writes → exception 01) |
| `vfd_basic` | holding | 0 control word (rw: 0 stop, 1 run, 4 reset), 1 setpoint ×0.01 Hz (rw 0–5000), 2 ramp time ×0.1 s (rw 1–600), 3 output freq ×0.01 Hz, 4 status bitfield (bit0 running, bit1 at speed, bit3 fault), 5 fault code, 6 motor current ×0.1 A | ramp at `50 Hz / ramp time`; current ∝ frequency; faults latch until reset while stopped |
| `temp_controller_basic` | holding | 0 PV i16 ×0.1 °C, 1 SP i16 ×0.1 °C (rw 0–1200), 2 output u16 ×0.1 % , 3 mode (rw 0 auto, 1 manual), 4 manual output ×0.1 % (rw 0–1000), 5 heater enable (rw 0/1) | `τ dPV/dt = ambient + gain·out − PV` (τ 60 s, gain 150 °C, ambient 25 °C); PI in auto |
| `energy_meter_basic` | input | 0 voltage f32 V, 2 current f32 A, 4 active power f32 W, 6 power factor f32, 8 frequency f32 Hz, 10 energy u32 ×0.01 kWh, 12 energy u64 Wh (ABCD) | sinusoidal load profile with noise; energy integrates power |

Fault codes, ranges and register maps are simulator design choices, not vendor documentation; the profiles say so.

## 6. Fault model

```rust
enum FaultKind { Timeout, CrcError, Exception(u8), Stale, WrongOrder, LateReply { delay_ms: u64 } }
enum Trigger { Always, Probability { per_mille: u16 }, Window { from_ms, until_ms }, Requests { skip: u32, count: u32 } }
struct FaultRule { unit: u8, kind: FaultKind, trigger: Trigger }
```

Probability draws come from a dedicated fault RNG seeded from the world seed, so a fault sequence is reproducible. Every probabilistic rule draws once per request to its unit, active or not. `Requests` counts requests per device. `Stale` needs a deterministic trigger (always, window, request count): it is evaluated while the process steps, where there is no request to draw for.

"Stale" means frozen process values while communication stays GOOD (a gateway serving a cache). Client-side STALE quality comes from age, so it is produced by timeouts and backoff, not by this fault; the training material explains both.
